Packing has resumed, but the supplier reports an ongoing backlog affecting both lines. The proposed consolidated shipment has not yet received a confirmed collection date.
Purchasing reviewed alternative sourcing options for this line. Samples received from another producer did not match the agreed flavour specification, so no replacement order was placed.
The supplier confirmed that its dispatch backlog remains unresolved and delivery delays are continuing. Purchasing requested written confirmation of cargo readiness before booking freight.
The supplier advised that a strike at its Korean dispatch warehouse was delaying export orders. Purchasing requested confirmation of which UK consignments could still be released.
The supplier confirmed that the degreaser order remained in the dispatch backlog. Its forwarder had not received the cargo, so the proposed sailing could not be confirmed.

Production of the floor wipes had finished, but warehouse disruption continued to delay loading. Purchasing asked the supplier to retain the agreed carton markings while arranging a revised collection.

The supplier reported that the strike had ended, although a significant export backlog remained unresolved. Purchasing requested confirmed cargo handover dates rather than provisional dispatch estimates.
The supplier advised that a backlog at its Korean consolidation warehouse is causing significant dispatch delays. Purchasing has requested revised sailing details for all outstanding UK orders.

The supplier confirmed that the JejuMandarinSparkle consignment missed its booked departure because warehouse picking was incomplete. Replacement vessel space has been requested but is not yet confirmed.

Packing of RoastedPearBarleyTea remains delayed while the supplier clears earlier export orders. We have asked for confirmation when the goods are ready for collection rather than a provisional dispatch date.

The supplier reported that the dispatch backlog remains unresolved and continues to affect UK-bound orders. Purchasing has requested a consolidated order update and written confirmation of each booking.
The supplier confirmed that export orders are consolidated at its Busan warehouse before shipment to the UK. Purchasing requested advance notice of any changes to the agreed dispatch schedule.
The revised samples passed our dimensional and finish checks. The supplier was authorised to use the approved packaging specifications for subsequent orders.
The supplier reported significant dispatch delays following industrial action at its packing contractor. Completed orders remain awaiting packing, and no revised departure dates have been confirmed.
The supplier advised that the packing backlog remains unresolved for both lines. Purchasing requested separate dispatches where cartons can be released without waiting for the rest of the order.
Purchasing issued an alternative sourcing brief covering dimensions, materials and retail packaging for both products. Any proposed substitute must pass sample approval before an order is placed.

The supplier confirmed that packing has resumed, but an ongoing backlog is still delaying export dispatches. Purchasing requested a confirmed carton release list and written booking confirmation from the forwarder.
Completed supplier onboarding for the Korean household cleaning range. Agreed that export orders would be consolidated at the supplier's Busan warehouse before shipment to the UK.
The supplier reported production delays following maintenance on its liquid filling line. Requested revised ready-for-collection dates for both products.
The export team advised that a warehouse labour dispute was disrupting order preparation and causing significant dispatch delays. Shipment bookings remain subject to confirmation.
The supplier confirmed that finished cartons were awaiting picking at its export warehouse. The ongoing strike has prevented it from committing to a collection date.

The warehouse strike remains unresolved and the supplier reports a substantial dispatch backlog. Purchasing has requested written confirmation of shipment readiness before authorising further freight bookings.
The supplier confirmed the regular monthly ordering schedule for shipments from Korea to the UK. Standard payment terms remain unchanged.
Both sauces arrived on the agreed delivery date. Quantities received matched the purchase order and the accompanying paperwork was complete.
The quarterly sales review recorded steady demand for both pastes. Purchasing retained the usual order frequency.
The supplier's latest quotation retained the existing unit prices across all four lines. Standard case sizes and ordering terms were also unchanged.
The scheduled consignment was received in full on the booked date. Batch details and best-before dates were entered into the purchasing records.
Sales of both sauces remained in line with their usual monthly pattern. The team maintained the established purchasing schedule.
The monthly supplier review recorded deliveries against the agreed schedule and invoices at the contracted prices. The next routine order was approved under the existing terms.
The supplier advised that a strike at its Korean cold-storage contractor is causing significant dispatch delays. Purchasing has requested revised sailing dates for all outstanding UK orders.
The dumpling order remains at the supplier's warehouse pending access to the contracted loading facility. The supplier has not confirmed an alternative dispatch arrangement.

The supplier confirmed that production is complete, but the rice bowl shipment is caught in the ongoing dispatch backlog. Purchasing asked for written confirmation of container allocation before accepting the revised shipment plan.

The supplier reported that loading has resumed, although the backlog remains unresolved and delivery dates are still subject to change. Purchasing will keep outstanding orders under review until vessel bookings are confirmed.
Supplier review completed with Onbit Wellness Foods in Korea. The agreed order-to-UK-delivery lead time remains eight weeks for its health food range.
Updated English-language artwork received for both products. Purchasing approved the outer-case labels for the next production run.

Onbit has announced that lead times for all four products will increase by three weeks, from eight to eleven weeks, for orders placed from 16 February. The supplier attributes the extension to reduced production capacity during equipment replacement.
Purchasing has updated the supplier planning record to the revised eleven-week lead time. Onbit confirmed that orders accepted before 16 February retain their previously agreed delivery dates.

The supplier confirmed that export orders for its kimchi and pickles are consolidated at its Busan warehouse before shipment to the UK. Purchasing has requested that packing lists continue to show batch codes and best-before dates.
The revised English-language labels for both kimchi lines have been approved. The supplier will introduce them on the next production batches without changing the recipes or case sizes.

The supplier advised that order-to-dispatch lead times for all three products will increase by four weeks, from six to ten weeks, for purchase orders placed from 16 February 2026. It attributed the change to reduced fermentation-room capacity during refurbishment; sea transit time is unchanged.

Purchasing confirmed that the additional four weeks applies to all new orders across the supplier's range. Orders accepted before 16 February retain their previously agreed dispatch dates, and the supplier has not yet confirmed when normal lead times will resume.
Completed the annual supplier review for this Korean kitchenware and storage manufacturer. Export carton specifications and UK delivery documentation remain unchanged.
Supplier confirmed approval of the revised English care labels for both products. The purchasing team has filed the artwork against the next production orders.

Seorin advised that lead times for all its products will increase by four weeks, from eight to twelve weeks, for purchase orders placed from 23 February. The supplier attributed the extension to reduced production capacity during a factory equipment upgrade.

Purchasing acknowledged the new twelve-week lead time for both products and requested revised dispatch dates for the next orders. Seorin confirmed that orders accepted before 23 February retain their previously agreed schedules.

Supplier review completed with Garam Personal Care Co. in Korea. The agreed order-to-dispatch lead time remains six weeks across its personal care range, with sea freight to the UK scheduled separately.
The supplier confirmed approval of the revised English-language packaging artwork for all three products. Purchasing filed the signed proofs against the relevant product records.

Garam announced that order-to-dispatch lead times will increase by four weeks, from six to ten weeks, for all its products on purchase orders placed from 9 February. The supplier attributed the change to reduced filling capacity during a factory refurbishment; sea freight transit times are unchanged.

Purchasing updated the supplier planning record to reflect the ten-week order-to-dispatch lead time. Garam confirmed that orders accepted before 9 February retain their previously agreed dispatch dates.
Completed the annual supplier review for this Korean milling and baking mix producer. Updated UK label artwork and ingredient specifications have been filed with purchasing.
The supplier confirmed that these three flours can be consolidated on the same export pallet. Purchase orders must retain separate batch references for each product.
Received revised outer carton specifications for the three baking blends and mixes. The supplier confirmed that recipes and retail pack weights are unchanged.

The supplier announced that lead times for all its products will increase by four weeks, from eight to twelve weeks from purchase order acceptance to arrival at our UK warehouse. The revised lead time applies to orders accepted from 16 February 2026, following reduced milling capacity during planned equipment replacement.
Purchasing acknowledged the revised twelve-week lead time and updated the supplier ordering calendar. The supplier has not provided a date for returning to the previous eight-week schedule.
Completed the annual supplier review for the Korean beverage and tea range. Requested updated product specifications and UK label proofs before the next production runs.

Receipt checks found that batch YPS251021 carried a Korean-only ingredients panel rather than the approved English label. The warehouse quarantined the entire received batch and blocked release; none had been dispatched to customers.
The supplier confirmed that domestic-market labels had been used during a packaging changeover. It supplied the batch packing records and agreed to fund replacement labels and UK reworking.

Technical approved the replacement English label against the signed product specification. The warehouse completed relabelling under quarantine, and Technical authorised release after checking the rework records and finished packs.

The supplier credited the agreed UK reworking costs and submitted a revised label-changeover procedure. Incident closure remains pending evidence that the new line-clearance and export-label checks have been used on the next UK production run.
Supplier review completed with the export team in Korea. Agreed that purchase orders would continue to be acknowledged within three working days, with batch specifications supplied before dispatch.
Updated UK label artwork approved for all three baking lines. The supplier confirmed that the revised labels would be applied from the next production run.

The supplier advised by email that lead times for all its products would increase by four weeks, from eight to twelve weeks, for purchase orders placed from 16 February. It attributed the change to reduced milling capacity during scheduled maintenance and longer bookings for export packing.

Purchasing updated the supplier lead-time record to twelve weeks and requested provisional production slots before raising new orders. The supplier confirmed that previously acknowledged orders would retain their agreed dispatch dates.
Completed the annual supplier review. The supplier confirmed that UK export orders continue to be consolidated at its Busan warehouse before shipment.

Approved the revised outer carton artwork following confirmation that the UK importer address and cooking instructions were correct. The supplier will use the revised cartons for orders packed from November.

The supplier advised that lead times for all products will increase by four weeks, from eight to twelve weeks, for purchase orders placed from 23 February. It attributed the extension to reduced packing capacity during a production-line refurbishment.

Purchasing confirmed that the additional four weeks applies to all three products, with no exceptions currently available. Existing accepted orders retain their previously confirmed dispatch dates; future orders will be planned against the twelve-week lead time.
Completed the annual supplier review for the Korean beverage producer. Updated food safety certification and UK importer contact details were received and filed.

Goods-in inspection found that the English labels on batch YOS260108 omitted sulphites, although the supplier's specification declared sulphur dioxide above 10 mg/l. The batch was quarantined and purchasing instructed the warehouse not to release it.

The supplier confirmed that an obsolete English label file had been used for batch YOS260108. Dispatch records confirmed that none of the affected batch had left our warehouse; the supplier agreed to fund compliant replacement labels and supervised relabelling.

Checked the tea labels against the approved specification following the sparkling drink incident. No discrepancies were found, and the supplier confirmed that the tea uses a separate label artwork file.

Quality approved the replacement label proof, including the sulphites declaration, but relabelling has not yet taken place. The batch remains on hold pending completion and inspection; the supplier's corrective action report and evidence of revised artwork controls are also outstanding.

Completed the annual supplier review for the Korean sauces and pastes range. The supplier provided its food safety certificate and confirmed that changes to recipes or UK labels require our written approval before production.

Goods-in checks found that batch SP251015 carried UK labels which omitted wheat from the allergen declaration, although wheat was listed in the approved specification. The batch was quarantined and further dispatches were stopped pending traceability checks.

Traceability checks confirmed that some cases from batch SP251015 had already been delivered to UK customers. We notified the relevant local authority, initiated a consumer recall and asked customers to remove the affected batch from sale and display the recall notice.

The supplier confirmed that an obsolete label file had been used during packing. It accepted responsibility for recall and relabelling costs and proposed controlled artwork access plus a second-person check at line start-up.
Reviewed retained UK labels against the approved specifications for both pastes following the sauce recall. No allergen declaration discrepancies were found.

Corrected labels for batch SP251015 were approved, and quarantined and returned units were relabelled by our UK contractor before QA release. Recall reconciliation was completed, with no reports of allergic reactions received.

The supplier's credit note for recall and relabelling costs has been received. The corrective action remains open because we are still awaiting evidence that obsolete artwork has been removed and the second-person label check has been implemented; the next shipment requires pre-dispatch label photographs and written QA approval.
Annual supplier review completed for the Korean seaweed and dried seafood range. Updated factory certification and UK export contact details were received and filed.

A customer reported that batch DS251006 had no English ingredients or allergen label on the retail packs. Inspection of retained samples confirmed the omission; the product specification lists squid and wheat as allergens.

Sales of batch DS251006 were stopped and warehouse staff were instructed to quarantine all remaining packs. Customers who had received the batch were told to stop sale and isolate affected packs pending recall instructions.

The technical team notified the local authority and issued a consumer recall notice identifying the batch and undeclared allergens. Purchasing sent the supplier the affected shipment references and requested a root-cause report and reimbursement of recall costs.

The supplier traced the omission to a missed UK labelling step after a packing-line changeover. Its corrective-action report proposes barcode verification and a signed first-pack check, but evidence that these controls have been implemented has not yet been supplied.

Recalled packs and quarantined packs from batch DS251006 were destroyed by the appointed contractor, and the destruction certificate was filed. All notified trade customers have confirmed completion of their recall actions.

The supplier's credit note for the affected goods has been received, but reimbursement of transport and destruction charges remains outstanding. Further shipments of this product remain on hold pending technical approval of the revised English label and evidence of the new packing checks.

Annual supplier review completed for the Korean noodles and rice range. Requested updated food safety certification and confirmation that all UK label changes require our written approval before production.

Goods-in inspection found that batch BSU251028 carried an English label which omitted sesame from the allergen declaration, although sesame was listed on the Korean packaging. The batch was placed on hold and dispatches were stopped pending confirmation of the affected quantity.

Traceability checks identified three UK trade customers who had received batch BSU251028. The technical team notified the relevant local authority and issued withdrawal instructions to customers, with recall notices for any packs already sold to consumers.

All three trade customers confirmed that remaining packs had been removed from sale and the recall notices displayed. Returned and warehouse-held packs remain segregated; no allergic reactions have been reported to us.

The supplier traced the omission to an obsolete English artwork file used by its packing contractor. It submitted corrected artwork and agreed to introduce version-controlled labels and a documented allergen check at line start-up.

Technical approved the corrected English artwork, but approval to resume dispatch remains withheld. The supplier still owes evidence that the new label checks have been implemented, a destruction certificate for affected packs and settlement of the agreed recall costs.

Supplier onboarding review completed for the Korean personal care factory. Requested finished-product microbiological specifications, batch release records and evidence of preservative efficacy testing before approving the first shipment.
Customer service reported an unusual sour odour in three body wash bottles and two shampoo bottles. Sent batch codes and photographs to the supplier and requested investigation of retained samples.

Two retailer complaints described separation and an altered smell in hand cream from batch RH2507. Quarantined the affected batch pending laboratory results and added it to the supplier's open quality investigation.

The factory audit found overdue calibration of the preservative dosing equipment and incomplete cleaning records on the shared filling line. The supplier could not demonstrate that these controls had been effective for all three products during the affected production period.

Independent testing found microbial counts above the agreed finished-product limits in samples from one batch of each product. Quality instructed purchasing to suspend new orders and hold unreleased consignments while the affected batch scope was confirmed.

Received the corrective action report covering dosing equipment calibration, revised cleaning verification and operator retraining. Requested supporting records and an independent follow-up audit; the report alone was not accepted as evidence for reinstatement.

The follow-up audit confirmed completion of equipment calibration and staff training, but cleaning verification records remained incomplete. Purchasing will not resume orders until Quality approves the outstanding evidence and satisfactory results from three consecutive production batches.

Annual supplier review completed for the Korean production site. Purchasing requested that changes to ingredients, allergens or packaging artwork receive written approval before production for the UK.

Goods-in inspection found that batch CCR251014 carried an English label which omitted milk from the allergen declaration, although the seasoning specification listed milk powder. The entire consignment was placed on hold and the supplier was asked to confirm the affected production scope.

Dispatch records confirmed that no units from batch CCR251014 had left our warehouse. The supplier confirmed that an obsolete English artwork file had been used and identified no other UK batches as affected.

Technical approved a corrective over-label declaring milk in bold, checked against the full ingredient specification. The supplier agreed to fund supervised relabelling and submit a corrective action report covering artwork version control.
Relabelling of batch CCR251014 was completed, with label reconciliation and inspection records signed off by Technical before release. Photographs and the completion report were sent to the supplier.

The supplier submitted a revised artwork approval procedure requiring independent checks before printing. Technical still requires evidence that obsolete files have been withdrawn and the first subsequent UK production run has passed the new checks; the corrective action remains open pending those records.
Two UK customers reported stale flavours and packs with partially open seals. We sent photographs and batch references to the supplier and requested an investigation.
Receipt inspection found weak seals on six packs from three outer cartons. The affected delivery was quarantined pending the supplier's assessment.

The packaging audit found incomplete seal-check records and no documented verification after sealing-jaw adjustments. The supplier was asked to submit a corrective action plan covering all snack and confectionery lines supplied to us.

The supplier attributed the sealing failures to worn sealing jaws and inconsistent temperature settings. Its corrective action plan included replacement parts, operator retraining and recorded hourly seal checks.

Further complaints about loss of crispness were received across all three products after the stated corrective action date. Retained samples included packs with leaking seals, and we requested an independent packaging assessment.

The independent assessment found that seal integrity testing was not consistently completed before dispatch. Purchasing agreed that future shipments would require batch-specific seal test reports and QA approval before release.

The supplier submitted revised inspection procedures and training records, but evidence of sustained compliance remains incomplete. QA has kept the corrective action open and requested records from three consecutive production runs.

Supplier onboarding review completed for the Korean health foods manufacturer. Requested its allergen control procedure, cleaning validation records and finished-product release specifications before approving the first orders.

Two UK customers reported hard particles in separate powder products. Retained samples and customer photographs were sent to the supplier for investigation, with batch traceability requested for both complaints.

Further complaints concerned a plastic fragment in a pouch of protein bites and visible sediment containing hard particles in a ginger shot. The supplier was asked to investigate these alongside the earlier powder complaints rather than treating each product separately.

The third-party site audit found incomplete foreign-body inspection records and no documented checks of brittle plastic fittings above open-product handling areas. Similar record gaps appeared on several production lines, indicating a site-wide control failure.

Purchasing suspended new orders pending technical approval of the corrective action plan. The supplier was instructed to replace damaged fittings, validate foreign-body controls for each product format and provide evidence of staff retraining.

The supplier submitted photographs of replacement fittings and revised inspection forms. Technical accepted the maintenance evidence but requested completed production records and independent verification before considering the corrective actions closed.

The follow-up review found that inspection records were still missing supervisor sign-off for batches covering all four products. Purchasing confirmed that new orders would remain suspended until the supplier demonstrated consistent implementation across the site.

Supplier onboarding review completed for the Korean kitchenware and storage range. Requested batch traceability records, material specifications and food-contact compliance documentation before approving repeat orders.

Customer returns included lunch boxes with loose lid clips and fridge tubs with poorly seated seals. Sent photographs and batch references to the supplier and requested an investigation into assembly checks.
Warehouse inspection found chipped jar rims, splintered tray edges and rough patches on bowl interiors across three separate batches. Affected cartons were quarantined pending supplier review.

The supplier audit found incomplete final inspection records and no documented procedure for controlling rejected goods. Inspectors also found that packaging checks were not consistently recorded across the range; a corrective action plan was requested.

The supplier submitted a corrective action plan covering inspector training, segregation of rejected goods and signed batch-release checks. Purchasing advised that photographs alone would not be accepted as evidence of effective implementation.

Independent pre-shipment inspection identified recurring finish defects and inconsistent lid fit across the five-product range. Shipment release was withheld, and the supplier was asked to sort the affected production and arrange reinspection.

Follow-up review found that corrective action records remained incomplete and complaint investigations had not established root causes. New purchase order approval remains suspended pending a satisfactory independent audit and evidence that revised controls are working.
Supplier review completed with the export team in Korea. Standard production lead time remains six weeks from purchase order confirmation, with sea freight booked separately.
A UK pharmacy chain has confirmed a listing for BirchDewFaceWash in 85 branches from November. Its opening order is 2,550 units, with replenishment to follow actual sell-through.

The UK online retailer has scheduled CamelliaSilkHandCream for a winter skincare promotion from 17 November to 14 December. It forecasts unit sales 30% above its usual four-week run rate during the promotion.
The pharmacy chain reported December sell-through 18% above its launch forecast for BirchDewFaceWash. It has raised its February and March replenishment forecast by 600 units per month.
The online retailer confirmed that the winter promotion ended as planned and will not be extended. Its March forecast for CamelliaSilkHandCream has returned to the pre-promotion monthly run rate.
Supplier review completed with the export team in Korea. Mixed-product orders remain available, with final case quantities to be confirmed before booking.
A UK grocery chain has confirmed a January listing for SeoulCrunchCabbageKimchi in 35 branches. Its opening order forecast is 420 cases, with repeat orders dependent on store sales.
The UK sales team has scheduled a four-week online promotion for GoldenRadishPickle starting on 12 January. The campaign forecast assumes unit sales 25% above the previous four-week period.

The grocery chain's first four weeks of sales for SeoulCrunchCabbageKimchi were 18% above its launch forecast, and it has requested a higher repeat order. GoldenRadishPickle promotion sales finished 22% above the preceding four weeks; the promotion has now ended.
Supplier review completed with the export team in Busan. Ulim confirmed that UK orders would continue to be consolidated into monthly sea freight departures.
A UK household retailer confirmed a listing for SoftCloudLaundrySheets in 45 shops from January 2026. Its initial forecast indicates additional demand of 900 packs per month for the first quarter.

The UK sales team agreed a spring-cleaning promotion with two regional retail chains for March and April. Their combined promotional forecast is 30% above normal monthly sales for CitrusFoamKitchenSpray.

The retailer reported January sales of 960 packs across the new listing and retained its 900-pack monthly forecast for February and March. Purchasing sent the revised UK demand plan to Ulim for production scheduling.
Supplier review: Ulsan Leaf & Beverage Co. confirmed that UK orders will continue to be consolidated at its Busan forwarder. Purchase orders must show the agreed English carton descriptions.
A UK grocery chain confirmed a listing for YujaHoneySpark in 48 shops from January 2026. Its opening order is separate from the proposed weekly replenishment schedule.

The grocery chain's first three weekly sales reports show YujaHoneySpark selling 28% above its launch forecast. The buyer has requested that we use the revised forecast for February replenishment planning.

Purchasing sent the supplier an updated YujaHoneySpark order forecast reflecting the UK retailer's stronger sales. The supplier acknowledged receipt and asked for firm quantities before reserving the next production slot.

The UK online retailer confirmed that its winter promotion for PearGingerInfusion ended on 15 February. It has reduced its March order forecast by 20% against February and does not plan to extend the promotional price.
Annual supplier review completed with the Busan sales office. Export orders continue to be consolidated through Busan, with order acknowledgements requested within three working days.
A UK homeware retailer has confirmed a January listing for NestSealLunchBox in 45 shops and online. Its initial order is for 2,700 units, with repeat orders dependent on weekly sales.
The supplier confirmed acceptance of the additional production quantity for the January retailer launch. UK barcode artwork has been approved for this order.
The retailer's first four weeks of sales were 24% above its launch forecast. Its buyer has requested weekly replenishment and asked us to use the revised sales forecast when planning March purchases.

Purchasing sent the revised March requirement to the supplier following the retailer's stronger launch sales. The supplier has been asked to confirm the earliest available production slot before we amend the purchase order.

Annual supplier review completed with the purchasing team in Korea. Verdami confirmed that UK export orders will continue to be consolidated at Busan, with English-language label artwork approved before production.

A UK health-food retailer has confirmed a January listing for JejuBarleyGreens and BlackSesameProtein across 42 shops and its website. Its initial forecast indicates additional monthly demand of 600 packs and 450 packs respectively, subject to launch performance.

The retailer has issued its opening purchase order for the January launch. Purchasing has asked Verdami to include the launch quantities in the next production booking; subsequent orders will be based on weekly sales.

The retailer's January sales report shows JejuBarleyGreens selling 18% above its launch forecast, while BlackSesameProtein is broadly in line with forecast. The retailer has revised its February and March JejuBarleyGreens requirement to 710 packs per month and left BlackSesameProtein at 450 packs.

Annual supplier review completed for the Korean milling site. Purchasing received updated food safety certification and agreed that changes to recipes or allergen handling must be notified before shipment.

An independent laboratory detected wheat gluten in a sample from batch CRF251001, which was labelled gluten-free. Quality instructed the warehouse to quarantine the batch and purchasing suspended further dispatches of this product pending investigation.

Distribution records confirmed that part of batch CRF251001 had reached UK customers. The incident lead notified the relevant enforcement authority and initiated a consumer recall, with notices identifying the affected batch and the undeclared wheat risk.

The supplier traced the contamination to shared packing equipment used after a wheat flour run without validated cleaning. It accepted responsibility for the affected batch and proposed dedicated packing utensils, revised cleaning procedures and gluten testing before release.

Quality reviewed the bread mix specification and UK artwork following the rice flour incident. Wheat was correctly declared, and the review identified no labelling correction required for this product.

Returned and quarantined units from the affected batch were destroyed by an authorised waste contractor, and the certificate was filed. The supplier issued a credit for the goods; reimbursement of recall and disposal costs remains under discussion.

Purchasing received revised cleaning instructions and staff training records, but the independent cleaning validation report is still outstanding. Shipment approval remains withheld until Quality accepts the validation evidence and satisfactory results for the proposed replacement batch; two trade customers have also yet to return their recall reconciliation forms.
Annual supplier review completed with the Korean export team. Araon confirmed that UK orders will continue to be consolidated into monthly frozen-container departures from Busan.
A UK grocery retailer has confirmed a listing for SeoulGardenKimchiDumplings in 45 stores from January. Its opening order is separate from the expected weekly replenishment orders.

The retailer's first three weeks of sales indicate that total UK weekly demand for SeoulGardenKimchiDumplings is approximately 30% above the October–December average. The buyer has asked us to use this higher rate for the next purchasing forecast.

Sent Araon the revised dumpling forecast following the retailer launch. The supplier confirmed that the additional volume can be included in the April production schedule if the purchase order is received by 27 February.
Annual supplier review completed. Woorim confirmed that UK orders are consolidated at its Busan warehouse and requested purchase orders six weeks before the required sailing.

The supplier reported a sharp increase in Korean supermarket orders following a domestic television promotion. It is reviewing export allocations for December production; this update concerns Korean demand, not UK sales.

Woorim reduced the quantity available against our January purchase order from 600 to 420 cartons, citing additional commitments to Korean retailers. The balance has been provisionally assigned to February production.
The supplier confirmed that the Korean ramyeon promotion has not affected production allocations for these two lines. Existing purchase order quantities and dispatch dates remain unchanged.

The outstanding 180 cartons were not included in the February production allocation. Woorim advised that continued Korean retail demand has extended the quoted order-to-dispatch lead time from six to nine weeks.
